sources.role: portable config default, PathEntries defaults, SaveRAM/savestate/movie naming, firmware scan

pinned controller config encoding: docs/BIZHAWK_SNES9X_CONTROLLER_CONTRACT.md, docs/BIZHAWK_GPGX_CONTROLLER_CONTRACT.md, docs/BIZHAWK_NESHAWK_CONTROLLER_CONTRACT.md, docs/BIZHAWK_PCEHAWK_CONTROLLER_CONTRACT.md, docs/BIZHAWK_SMSHAWK_CONTROLLER_CONTRACT.md, docs/BIZHAWK_TURBONYMA_CONTROLLER_CONTRACT.md; Unix BIZHAWK_HOME/BIZHAWK_DATA_HOME in docs/BIZHAWK_DEFINITION_CAPTURE.md

paths.path: config.ini in the EmuHawk program directory (portable); Program.cs falls back to PathUtils.ExeDirectoryPath/config.ini when no --config argument is given. The file is JSON-formatted despite the .ini name (ConfigService uses Newtonsoft.Json). Controller bindings live in the AllTrollers map keyed by per-system deck names (SNES Controller, NES Controller, GPGX Genesis Controller, PC Engine Controller) with P<n> <button> keys, alongside AllTrollersAnalog/AllTrollersFeedbacks/AllTrollersAutoFire; per-core port and device settings sit under CoreSyncSettings.<full core type name> (e.g. BizHawk.Emulation.Cores.Nintendo.SNES9X.Snes9x); core choice is PreferredCores.<SYSTEM> with DontTryOtherCores; the PathEntries table in the same file holds every path override (%exe%/%rom% and per-system Base supported)

Per-system Save RAM directory from the PathEntries table: default ./SaveRAM under each system Base, resolving to <programdir>/<System dir>/SaveRAM (e.g. <programdir>/SNES/SaveRAM); NDS, Atari 2600, AmstradCPC, Channel F, Coleco and Doom omit Save RAM by default
paths.naming: <rom FilesystemSafeName>.SaveRAM with a .SaveRAM.bak written alongside. Two-slot model: with AutosaveSaveRAM enabled, periodic flushes write <name>.AutoSaveRAM.SaveRAM while normal saves write <name>.SaveRAM, and LoadSaveRam picks the newer of the two (prompting when the autosave is newer); while a movie is active both names gain a .<movie filename without extension> suffix before .SaveRAM, isolating movie play from normal play

paths.path: Per-system Savestates directory from PathEntries: default ./State under each system Base, resolving to <programdir>/<System dir>/State (e.g. <programdir>/SNES/State); movies go to the global Movies entry (default <programdir>/Movies) with backups in Movies/backup
paths.naming: <rom FilesystemSafeName>.<CoreName>.QuickSave<N>.State where N = slot % 10 (slots 1-10; slot 10 writes QuickSave0); the prefix additionally carries the bsnes profile and, while a movie is active, .<movie filename without extension>; Save State As writes arbitrary .State files; movies are .bk2 files (Bk2Movie.Extension = bk2)

paths.path: Global Firmware directory from PathEntries: default <programdir>/Firmware; FirmwareManager.DoScanAndResolve scans that directory and EmuHawk opens its firmware manager (Config > Firmware) when a core needs a missing file
paths.naming: Per-system firmware files: FDS disksys.rom, PCE CD PCECDBIOS.pce, Colecovision ColecoBios.bin, GBA gbabios.rom, Atari Lynx BIOS, TI-83 ti83_107.rom, SNES coprocessor ROMs (cx4.rom, dsp1b.rom, st010.rom, sgb.sfc etc.), PlayStation ps-30a.bin/ps-30e.bin/ps-30j.bin, Sega CD/Saturn and SMS regional BIOSes, 7800/Intellivision/C64/Apple IIe files; none are distributed with BizHawk

windows.notes: Primary platform: EmuHawk.exe from GitHub releases (README requires at least Win10 22H2 or Win11 21H2; a 1.13.2 backport exists for XP/7/8.1). Lunchbox launches with a private --config copy and leaves PathEntries-directed save/state locations untouched.

paths.path: config.ini in the effective EmuHawk installation directory (portable); Program.cs falls back to PathUtils.ExeDirectoryPath/config.ini, and at the pinned revision the Unix PathExtensions derives that directory from BIZHAWK_HOME (and the data directory from BIZHAWK_DATA_HOME) when set. Same JSON layout as Windows: AllTrollers deck maps, CoreSyncSettings, PreferredCores, PathEntries

linux.notes: Supported: bizhawk-monort release started with EmuHawkMono.sh (runtime deps glibc, Mono complete, OpenAL, Lua 5.4); README calls the port about at parity with Mupen64Plus (N64) the notable omission, in a Windows-centric project. Lunchbox's direct-Mono launch supplies BIZHAWK_HOME/BIZHAWK_DATA_HOME explicitly and passes a private --config copy (docs/BIZHAWK_DEFINITION_CAPTURE.md).

paths.path: Legacy only: config.ini in the EmuHawk program directory, same portable layout as Windows (Program.cs ExeDirectoryPath/config.ini fallback; JSON-formatted file with AllTrollers/CoreSyncSettings/PreferredCores/PathEntries); current BizHawk does not run on macOS, so only the legacy 1.x port or the old 2.x source fork use this layout there
evidence: readme:macOS (legacy BizHawk) section at the pinned commit

paths.path: Legacy only: per-system Save RAM directory, default ./SaveRAM under each system Base relative to the program directory (e.g. <programdir>/SNES/SaveRAM)
paths.naming: <rom FilesystemSafeName>.SaveRAM (+ .SaveRAM.bak); autosave slot <name>.AutoSaveRAM.SaveRAM chosen over the normal slot when newer; movie-active names gain a .<movie filename without extension> suffix before .SaveRAM

paths.path: Legacy only: per-system Savestates directory, default ./State under each system Base (e.g. <programdir>/SNES/State); movies in the global Movies directory (default <programdir>/Movies)
paths.naming: <rom FilesystemSafeName>.<CoreName>.QuickSave<N>.State with N = slot % 10; Save State As writes .State files; movies are .bk2

paths.path: Legacy only: global Firmware directory, default <programdir>/Firmware, scanned by the firmware manager
paths.naming: Same firmware set as Windows (disksys.rom, gbabios.rom, ps-30a/e/j.bin etc.); not distributed with BizHawk

macos.notes: macOS support level: none for current releases. The README section macOS (legacy BizHawk) lists the options: use Windows/Linux or an x86_64 VM, run Sappharad's older 1.x port via Rosetta, or build his old 2.x source fork; Apple silicon would need x86_64 plus Rosetta. Paths above follow the pinned source's platform-independent exe-relative layout and apply to those legacy builds.
